source: OpenCV vtest.avi, all 795 decoded frames, 10 FPS; zero-based frame indices.
method: Independent visual review of raw frames at 20-frame intervals across the complete clip, closer boundary crops and detailed occlusion frames. Appearance and continuous paths used to deduplicate repeated crossings. Not derived from tracker IDs.
countConvention: Count every distinct visibly human person across the complete image, including partial boundary appearances, distant upper-path person and person at car boot. Count recurring/reentering participants once. Exclude vehicles, tripod and signs.
scope: Manual visual count for this clip, not independently labelled MOT benchmark ground truth. Frame bounds are nearest reviewed appearances and may differ slightly from the first/last visible pixel; P12 firstFrame is approximate.

idSwitch.observation: Same brown/dark jacket and blue-jeans person is beside/behind the central sign in the before frame and emerges to its left in the after frame; tracked ID changes from75 to100.
idSwitch.explanation: The sign and lamp pole hide much of the body while another black-clothed person crosses nearby. These occlusions plausibly disrupted motion/box-overlap association; this cause is an interpretation, not an internal tracker diagnosis.
